name: Pod resources: requests, limits & scheduling
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling. Resource requests drive scheduling (the scheduler places a pod only where its requests fit a node's allocatable); limits cap usage; together they set the pod's QoS class. Set requests/limits on a workload, then diagnose a pod stuck Pending because its request exceeds every node.

questions.title: Set requests and limits (QoS)
questions.teach:
`resources.requests` is what the scheduler **reserves** on a node (and what it schedules against); `resources.limits` is the hard cap the kubelet enforces (CPU throttled, memory OOM-killed). Requests ≠ limits ⇒ the pod's **QoS class is `Burstable`** (equal requests==limits for every resource ⇒ `Guaranteed`; none set ⇒ `BestEffort`).

**Gotcha:** CPU is **compressible** (over-limit = throttled); memory is **not** (over-limit = OOMKilled). The scheduler only looks at **requests**, never limits.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `resources-learn`, create a Deployment `rated` (1 replica, image `nginx:1.25`) whose container `web` sets requests `cpu=100m, memory=64Mi` and limits `cpu=250m, memory=128Mi`.

Target: Deployment `rated` is ready; its container has those exact requests/limits, giving QoS class `Burstable`.
questions.hint: Put `resources: { requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}, limits: {cpu: 250m, memory: 128Mi} }` on the container. Check QoS with `kubectl -n resources-learn get pod -l app=rated -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.qosClass}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl create namespace resources-learn 2>/dev/null
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: rated, namespace: resources-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: rated } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: rated } }
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:1.25
        resources:
          requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi }
          limits:   { cpu: 250m, memory: 128Mi }
YAML
kubectl -n resources-learn rollout status deploy/rated

verification.description: Deployment rated ready with requests 100m/64Mi, limits 250m/128Mi (QoS Burstable)

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod stuck Pending (request too big)
questions.teach:
A pod whose CPU/memory **request exceeds every node's allocatable** can never be placed — it sits `Pending` with a scheduler event `0/N nodes are available: Insufficient cpu`. The fix is on the workload: lower the request to something a node can satisfy.

**Gotcha:** this is a **request** problem, not limits — the scheduler rejects it before it ever runs. `kubectl describe pod` Events name the exact shortfall.
questions.prompt:
Setup created Deployment `hog` in `resources-learn` requesting `cpu: "6"` — more than any node's 4 allocatable CPUs — so its pod is `Pending`. Diagnose and fix it so `hog` runs (keep it reasonable, e.g. `cpu: 200m`).

Target: Deployment `hog` has 1 ready replica and its container's CPU request is ≤ 1 core.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n resources-learn describe pod -l app=hog` → 'Insufficient cpu'. Lower the request: `kubectl -n resources-learn patch deploy hog --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/cpu","value":"200m"}]'` (or edit the Deployment).
questions.solution:
kubectl -n resources-learn patch deploy hog --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/cpu","value":"200m"}]'
kubectl -n resources-learn rollout status deploy/hog

verification.description: Deployment hog scheduled & ready after reducing its CPU request
